**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Bluefly, which meets the playbook's **preferred** position.

What I checked and why each is benign:

- **§ 14.16 Freedom of Action** — "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others." Mutual and permissive; it affirmatively preserves our freedom rather than restricting it.
- **§ 14.11 No Resale** — "Customer shall not resell the Services, in whole or in part." A restriction on reselling IBM's own Services, not on the businesses we operate or products we build or buy. Standard and outside the scope of this rule.
- **§ 12.1 / § 14.17** — Base Components licensed "solely in connection with the Services" and no implied licences. Ordinary licence-grant boundaries, not restrictive covenants.
- **§ 14.19 Geographic Scope** — Limits *IBM's* delivery and obligations to the United States. No territorial restriction on us.
- **§ 13.2 Acceptable Use Policy** — Contains only IBM's modification right; no field-of-use restriction.

Targeted searches for "compet", "exclusiv", "restrict", "similar services", "engage in", and "Customer shall not" returned nothing that binds us to a competitive or field-of-use restraint. The planner's expectation that this rule would be absent is confirmed.
